scenario: An independent recruiter receives one referral note, creates an explicit person and Growth Lead relationship from Chat, asks what to remember before the first call, receives a source-linked no_action brief, opens a staged page change for review, cancels a second contact draft, and reloads the relationship URL.
frozen_evidence: 18 Web test files and 79 tests passing
Successful Next.js production build with 22 generated routes
Live browser DOM receipts for contact draft opened, draft canceled, source-linked brief compiled, no_action, and relationship recovery after reload

review_plan.reason: The artifact changes the default daily workflow for an independent recruiter.
The Agent can create internal relationship objects and navigate evidence and action surfaces.
The workspace contains explicit responsive and mobile-first Agent behavior.
The artifact does not assess, compare, rank, score, or recommend candidate quality.
The reviewed slice does not send candidate-facing communication or execute an external candidate action.

findings.criterion: Action usefulness and Agent command coverage
findings.observation: The live Web build recognizes five narrow English and Chinese page commands, opens a governed contact draft from Chat, navigates to structured review, and returns a visible operation state. It does not yet compose multi-step recruiter work or expose a durable server-side capability run.
findings.evidence: Live local relationship URL; apps/web/lib/agent-ui-command.ts; apps/web/lib/agent-ui-command.test.ts; browser DOM status 'Agent opened a governed contact draft.'
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can operate the current person without leaving Chat, but requests outside the small command grammar fall back to a brief and cannot yet coordinate a longer preparation task.
findings.recommendation: Promote the same five commands into versioned typed capabilities with an operation proposal and receipt contract, then add one bounded multi-step job only after usage evidence identifies it.
findings.verification: Run create-person, add-source, review-changes, open-person, and open-next-move from free text; each must identify the affected object, preserve authority, survive reload where appropriate, and never execute an external write.

findings.observation: The created person, relationship context, governed source, and reloadable URL survive a full refresh. The current Chat answer and page-operation receipt are transient and must be recompiled after reload.
findings.evidence: The synthetic contact and Growth Lead search reloaded from the same person and context IDs; the Chat answer was absent after reload and recompiled successfully from the persisted source ledger.
findings.user_impact: The important relationship state is safe, but a recruiter returning after an interruption cannot see the last Agent request or whether a local navigation command was recently completed.
findings.recommendation: Persist a compact relationship task history containing objective, typed operation, affected object, snapshot, status, and safe replay affordance without treating the conversation transcript as truth.
findings.verification: Create a contact, ask a brief, reload, and return after a simulated day; the person and source remain current, the last task receipt is visible, and replay creates no duplicate person or source.

findings.observation: The executable scenario reduces navigation and duplicate entry, but it uses synthetic data and returns an intentional no_action from one minimal recruiter note.
findings.evidence: talent-signal-agent-final-e2e-v2.png shows one Agent pane, one living person page, source-linked brief cards, and no_action; no working-recruiter comparison is attached.
findings.user_impact: The product direction is coherent, but the claimed reduction in pre-call reconstruction and missed timing is not yet established in real recruiter work.
findings.recommendation: Run a five-minute pre-call comparison with independent recruiters using their current chat, notes, and files fallback against this workspace.
findings.verification: For at least five consented cases, measure time to recover the current dependency, seeded-error correction, duplicate entry, changed-next-action rate, and willingness to reuse.

strengths: Chat stays beside the affected person instead of competing with People and Sources as another record.
Creating a contact requires an explicit person, relationship context, and first governed source.
The Agent can navigate and stage internal work while fact review and consequential action remain structured.
The source-linked answer can return no_action instead of manufacturing urgency.
The workspace does not score or rank the person.
missing_evidence: Working-recruiter comparison against the current manual fallback.
Persisted Agent task and operation receipts across reload and day-later return.
Measured completion and correction rates for natural-language page commands.
A real mobile build completing create, capture, review, and resume.
open_questions: Which one multi-step recruiter job occurs often enough to justify expanding beyond the five current page capabilities?
Should a recent Agent task receipt appear in the living page timeline or in a lightweight relationship task history?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The current Agent recognizes a closed client-side command grammar and maps it only to navigation, source intake, contact drafting, page review, and next-move navigation. The operation proposal and receipt are not yet enforced by a server-side capability registry.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/agent-ui-command.ts returns one of five typed commands or null; external effects remain outside runAgentUiCommand; ADR 0005 rejects arbitrary DOM automation.
findings.user_impact: The current build cannot silently message or schedule from Chat, but a future command added only in the client could drift from authorization, audit, and replay rules.
findings.recommendation: Define a versioned capability request containing actor, purpose, person, relationship context, command, affected object, expected version, consequence class, and idempotency key.
findings.verification: Fuzz ordinary questions and unsupported commands, tamper with IDs, repeat idempotency keys, and request external writes; only scoped allowed commands may proceed and consequential requests must stop at approval.

findings.observation: The Agent contact form explicitly creates a new person from a recruiter-entered name, context, and first source. It does not silently merge, but it does not show same-name or confirmed-handle candidates before creation.
findings.evidence: AgentCreatePersonCard submits scope_mode 'new_person' and states that it does not guess, merge, or contact anyone; the live submission created one explicit person and context.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can intentionally create a duplicate person and later face split evidence and reconciliation work.
findings.recommendation: Before final creation, run deterministic account-scoped identity narrowing and show possible existing people with exact match reasons while preserving create-new and leave-unresolved.
findings.verification: Seed two same-name people and one exact confirmed handle; the form must never auto-merge, must show the exact-handle candidate, and must preserve a reversible decision.

findings.observation: Relationship data and sources persist with registered deletion paths, while the current Agent page-operation receipt is transient UI state and is not part of the append-only task history.
findings.evidence: A full reload restored the created person, context, and source but removed the recent local command receipt.
findings.user_impact: No evidence truth is lost, but a returning recruiter cannot distinguish whether Chat recently navigated, staged, canceled, or completed an internal operation.
findings.recommendation: Store compact operation events separately from evidence and confirmed relationship state, with purpose, object, status, cancellation, and retention semantics.
findings.verification: Complete, cancel, reload, and delete each internal command scenario; the timeline must retain the allowed audit event and never promote the receipt to a person fact.

strengths: Chat is scoped to one explicit person and relationship context.
Contact creation requires recruiter-owned source material and does not infer, merge, or contact anyone.
Page changes remain staged and visible on the affected object before confirmation.
Generated briefs retain snapshot and Context Manifest identifiers with governed reference counts.
No Agent command can currently send, schedule, update an external contact, or claim an unverified external result.
The UI distinguishes no_action from failure and prevents prohibited person inference.
missing_evidence: Server-enforced Agent capability registry and durable operation receipts.
Possible-duplicate identity review inside the Agent create flow.
Cross-tenant and permission-change tests for Agent commands.
Mobile accessibility inspection of evidence and approval surfaces.
Field privacy and retention comprehension testing with recruiters.
open_questions: Which internal Agent operations should be stored as audit events, and which navigation-only operations should remain ephemeral?
What exact identity evidence is sufficient to suggest an existing person without creating pressure to merge?

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The 390-pixel structural prototype demonstrates an Agent-first viewport and transition to the person page, and production CSS contains explicit responsive fallbacks. The authenticated production build was not successfully exercised at a real 390-pixel viewport.
findings.evidence: workspace-concept-a-mobile-chat.png and workspace-concept-a-mobile-page.png; apps/web/app/globals.css media queries; desktop executable build for the final production artifact.
findings.user_impact: The intended mobile hierarchy is plausible, but clipping, keyboard avoidance, nested scrolling, browser chrome, and real touch behavior remain unproven.
findings.recommendation: Run the production flow on small and large iPhone viewports and an iOS Simulator, including create contact, add source, ask Agent, review a long fact, background, and resume.
findings.verification: At 390 pixels and on the smallest supported iPhone, complete the task with no horizontal overflow, hidden action, nested-scroll trap, keyboard obstruction, or loss after interruption.

findings.observation: The production mobile shell now uses a 64-pixel bottom bar, 44-pixel primary targets, visible Agent, People, and Sources labels, and a 44-pixel Agent composer action. The final rendered mobile surface has not been visually inspected after this correction.
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/globals.css sets bottom navigation and Agent actions to at least 44 pixels; mobile prototype screenshots show the intended composition.
findings.user_impact: The code meets minimum target geometry, but content expansion or safe-area insets may still compress labels or place controls near the home indicator.
findings.recommendation: Add safe-area padding, inspect localization expansion, and test labels and targets with touch visualization on real device sizes.
findings.verification: Agent, People, Sources, add-source, theme, and Ask Agent remain distinct and tappable at 200 percent text expansion with safe-area inset.

findings.observation: The DOM exposes labeled regions, controls, status announcements, and non-color states. Dynamic Type, VoiceOver order, focus return, dark mode, slow network, and offline recovery were not directly tested for this shell.
findings.evidence: Browser DOM snapshots expose the Agent, person page, governed sources, operation status, and live status text; production CSS includes reduced-motion behavior.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader or large-text user may encounter a different hierarchy than the visual prototype, and a slow response may leave the small viewport without enough context.
findings.recommendation: Run the mobile matrix at default, XXXL, AX3, and AX5 with VoiceOver, reduced motion, dark mode, slow network, and background or foreground transitions.
findings.verification: The critical path is announced in evidence-to-action order, focus lands on the affected object after navigation, progress is honest, and recovery creates no duplicate write.

strengths: Chat occupies the first mobile viewport without replacing the person page.
Bottom navigation preserves direct access to Agent, People, and Sources with visible labels.
Critical mobile targets are coded at 44 pixels or larger.
The interface uses text in addition to color for staged, completed, no-change, confirmed, and no-action states.
The layout uses 100dvh-aware sizing and reduced-motion behavior.
missing_evidence: Authenticated production build at 390 pixels and on real iPhone sizes.
VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, keyboard, safe-area, localization, and focus-order results.
Slow-network, offline, cancellation, and interruption recovery.
Dark-mode visual inspection of the redesigned workspace.
Real-device evidence for screenshot intake and evidence review.
open_questions: Should mobile return to the last selected Agent or People surface, or always start in Agent for a relationship URL?
Which operation receipt needs to remain visible above the keyboard after a Chat-triggered page action?

top_findings.reason: The current closed command grammar is safe, but future Agent operations need one server-enforced capability and receipt boundary.
top_findings.next_step: Implement a versioned internal Agent capability request and durable operation receipt before adding another state-changing command.
top_findings.verification: Tampering, replay, unsupported-command, cross-context, and external-write tests must stop outside the model and preserve exact approval boundaries.

top_findings.reason: The mobile direction is supported by prototype and code, not by an authenticated production run with accessibility and interruption evidence.
top_findings.next_step: Run the production build through the relevant mobile test matrix on a 390-pixel viewport and iOS Simulator.
top_findings.verification: Create, ask, navigate, review, interrupt, and resume with no clipping, inaccessible control, scroll trap, or duplicate action.

top_findings.reason: The executable synthetic loop is coherent but does not prove that working recruiters prepare faster or preserve more momentum.
top_findings.next_step: Run a timed five-minute pre-call comparison with independent recruiters and their current fallback.
top_findings.verification: The product must reduce reconstruction or correction burden without reducing evidence accuracy or user control.

agreements: All selected reviewers agree that the person within a relationship context remains the canonical working object and Chat should operate beside it rather than become the record.
All selected reviewers agree that the current Agent must stay narrow, typed, source-aware, reversible, and unable to execute consequential external writes.
All selected reviewers agree that the desktop local slice is materially stronger than peer Chat, People, and Sources destinations.
All selected reviewers agree that production and commercial claims require mobile and field evidence beyond the current synthetic local proof.

disagreements.issue: How much Agent history should persist after reload

positions.position: Persist the last task and operation receipt so the recruiter can resume without reconstructing Agent work.
positions.evidence: The relationship reloaded correctly while the recent Chat answer and canceled-draft receipt disappeared.

positions.position: Do not persist an unbounded Chat transcript or allow an operation receipt to become relationship truth.
positions.evidence: Conversation and operation text can contain sensitive data and has different authority and retention from evidence and confirmed state.

disagreements.resolution: Persist compact typed task events with objective reference, affected object, snapshot, state, and retention policy; keep free-form transcript content ephemeral by default.
disagreements.resolution_basis: This preserves recruiter continuity without flattening runtime conversation into evidence or permanent person memory.

adjudication.rationale: The local desktop slice passes as a direction and executable prototype: contact creation, governed source attachment, typed page commands, source-linked Chat, no_action, staged page review, cancellation, and reload recovery are observable. It is not ready for a production or commercial pass because the capability boundary is still client-local, responsive evidence is below release level, and recruiter value is not field-tested.

next_tests.test: Server-enforced internal Agent capability and receipt contract
next_tests.evidence_required: Executable create-person, add-source, review-changes, open-person, and open-next-move cases plus tamper, replay, cross-context, and prohibited external-write cases.
next_tests.pass_condition: Every allowed operation is scoped, typed, idempotent where state changes, and visible; unsupported or consequential effects cannot bypass review.

next_tests.evidence_required: Screenshots, VoiceOver output, focus order, interruption state, and recovery results on 390-pixel and iOS Simulator runs.
next_tests.pass_condition: The complete Agent-to-person-to-review loop remains legible, operable, and recoverable with no accessibility veto or duplicate effect.

next_tests.evidence_required: Consented cases, current-fallback baseline, time, corrections, missed dependency, changed-next-action, repeat-use, and qualitative trust evidence.
next_tests.pass_condition: The workspace reduces reconstruction or missed timing without increasing unsupported confirmation, privacy concern, or reconciliation work.
